summary: a bear crossing Boulder Canyon (SH 119) into heavy Saturday-afternoon traffic caused the car ahead of a pickup truck to stop suddenly; the truck rear-ended it and flipped over the embankment into Boulder Creek running ~4x average flow on peak spring runoff; the father and his twin daughter climbed out and reached shore but 13-year-old Sophia DuBose was swept downstream; dive teams and personnel from 12+ agencies ran downstream rescue operations for ~90 minutes until she was pulled from the creek behind Boulder High School ~6 p.m., not breathing, and she later died at the hospital; Boulder Canyon closed ~3 hours during the rescue
location: Boulder Canyon (SH 119), Boulder Creek (recovered behind Boulder High School)
responding_agency: Boulder County Sheriff's Office; dive teams and personnel from 12+ agencies
notes: Mountain-Ear story 1766 (parent-opened); date pinned by Saturday-afternoon crash + Sunday school memorial + Thursday June 5 memorial service (weekday-verified); twin sister and father escaped uninjured; memorial fund via Wild Bear
